correctness.rationale: Source-by-source inclusion-exclusion yields exact detection probability, and independently checked adjacent exchanges reduce global placement optimality to one monotone boundary quantity. Strict parameter inequalities, boundary tie multiplicity, one interior root, and asymptotic scaling follow analytically. The embedded exact-rational verifier checks all source/bond outcomes for 360 choices, plus adjacent exchanges and the 4-vertex witness; no finite test is used to prove the all-n theorem.

Compared semantic implications with prior epidemic percolation and sensor surveillance papers and published-finding corpus nearest hits; no known stronger statement directly subsumes this different probability objective. Bibliographic nonexhaustiveness is disclosed.

value.rationale: Ever-detection probability is an actionable distinct surveillance criterion, and the all-path-length exact optimizer transition is nontrivial: endpoints are suboptimal for most rates but uniquely optimal sufficiently close to p=1. The exact threshold and its 2/(n-2)^2 scaling provide a motivated structural law, not a narrow enumerated curiosity. Explicit tie classification and minimum n=4 example further clarify the boundary.
